title: Marijuana and Fortune; drugs in corporations
summary: Maxwell tried pot after reading about Muggles.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You know, I don't know, maybe some of the young kids -- I know, when I was young I read an article in Fortune Magazine. Somebody said, how'd you ever come to smoke marijuana -- this was the days before everybody did it. And I smoked it sometimes, you know. I said, well, to tell you the truth, I got the idea out of Fortune Magazine. Luce publications -- there was an article about Louis Armstrong. He made a record called "Muggles" and they said muggles is a marijuana cigarette which, "it is reputed Mr. Armstrong owes his inspiration to." I thought, aha, that's it. That's how he does it. So I ran out and bought a joint now for somebody.
And Life Magazine Corporation got me started smoking marijuana. Henry Luce got me hooked.
I just had to smoke long enough to skip four bars on the bridge of "Sweet and Lovely" and I gave up.

Nor for me. I just smoked a joint and wouldn't cross a street for a whole day. I'd see two cars down the street, I said, "I'll never make it." I stayed right there. I said, if I can just come down this time, they'll have no more trouble with me.

I knew some guy who insisted on keeping it up, he kept smoking it. Actually, I think that's probably one of the most overrated things in the world, smoking pot. I'd much rather have a drink of whiskey.

This guy, though, all the years, I think he wanted to keep a hip image or something, from smoking pot. I noticed his eyes got clear all of a sudden and I said, "what happened, don't you smoke any more?" He said, "no, I gave it up, the kids got all the good stuff." He said, he can't buy it any more, the kids got it all. The secretaries -- I have a friend who works for a corporation on Fifth Avenue, and this guy gets something like a pound of pot every week delivered up there. Eight ounces of cocaine. It's a business company and they pass it out like scotch.

They're hawking it all up and down Sixth Avenue in New York City at lunchtime. The guys just stand out there on the parkways, they're standing out there hawking it like they're selling hot dogs. (Inaudible). "Smoke, anybody, good smokes here."
Oh, yeah, I've heard guys say that.
I never paid much attention to them. That's what they're talking about?
And you can get you a complete high at noon, absolutely.
But these top corporations, they're passing the junk out like -- it used to be they had the bar with the scotch and soda. Now it's coke and pot.
Amazing. And yet we're the ones that get all the (inaudible).
Hell, we can't even afford it.
